questions.q: Choose the phrase with the correct order of adjectives: 'They live in ____.'
questions.x: Correct answer: a large white wooden house. Order: size – colour – material.

questions.q: He hardly ever comes late, ____?
questions.x: Correct answer: does he. 'Hardly' is negative in sense, so the tag is positive.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
Not only the employees / but also the manager / were present at the hearing.
questions.x: The error is in part (c): 'were present at the hearing'. With 'not only … but also', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'manager': 'was present'.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive form: 'The committee will review the proposal next week.'
o: The proposal would be reviewed by the committee next week.
The proposal will be reviewed by the committee next week.
The proposal will have been reviewed by the committee next week.
The proposal is being reviewed by the committee next week.
questions.x: Correct answer: The proposal will be reviewed by the committee next week.. Future simple passive: will be + past participle.

questions.q: In the sentence 'The minister's perfunctory inspection of the site lasted barely ten minutes', the word 'perfunctory' most nearly means:
o: Done carelessly as a mere formality
questions.x: Correct answer: Done carelessly as a mere formality. Perfunctory: done with minimum effort.

questions.q: The strike was ____ after the management accepted the demands.
questions.x: Correct answer: called off. 'Call off' means cancel.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
The reason for his absence / was because / he had fallen ill.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'was because'. Use 'the reason … was that'; 'because' repeats the idea of reason.

questions.q: In the sentence 'The two departments are at loggerheads over the budget', the idiom means:
questions.x: Correct answer: In strong disagreement. At loggerheads: in dispute.

questions.q:
Choose the best replacement for the bracketed part of the sentence. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
No sooner did the bell ring (when) the workers rushed to the gate.
questions.x: 'No sooner … than' is the correct pairing.

questions.q:
Choose the best replacement for the bracketed part of the sentence. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
Each of the workers (was given) a safety helmet.
questions.x: Correct answer: No improvement. 'Each of' takes a singular verb.

questions.q: According to the author, an institution's integrity is best judged by:
o: Whether wrongdoing ever occurs within it
The number of laws it follows
How it treats people who expose wrongdoing
questions.x: Answer: 'How it treats people who expose wrongdoing'. This is the final sentence. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Organisations often say they welcome criticism, yet the person who reports wrongdoing frequently pays the highest price. Whistleblowers lose promotions, face transfers, or are quietly isolated by colleagues who prefer peace to truth. A law that protects them on paper is of little use if the process of complaint is slow and the identity of the complainant leaks. The test of an institution's integrity is not whether wrongdoing ever occurs, but how it treats those who bring it to light.

questions.q: The phrase 'colleagues who prefer peace to truth' refers to people who:
o: Avoid conflict even at the cost of ignoring wrongdoing
questions.x: Answer: 'Avoid conflict even at the cost of ignoring wrongdoing'. They isolate the whistleblower to avoid disturbance. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Organisations often say they welcome criticism, yet the person who reports wrongdoing frequently pays the highest price. Whistleblowers lose promotions, face transfers, or are quietly isolated by colleagues who prefer peace to truth. A law that protects them on paper is of little use if the process of complaint is slow and the identity of the complainant leaks. The test of an institution's integrity is not whether wrongdoing ever occurs, but how it treats those who bring it to light.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a cost faced by whistleblowers?
questions.x: Answer: 'Criminal prosecution'. Prosecution is not mentioned in the passage. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Organisations often say they welcome criticism, yet the person who reports wrongdoing frequently pays the highest price. Whistleblowers lose promotions, face transfers, or are quietly isolated by colleagues who prefer peace to truth. A law that protects them on paper is of little use if the process of complaint is slow and the identity of the complainant leaks. The test of an institution's integrity is not whether wrongdoing ever occurs, but how it treats those who bring it to light.

questions.q: According to the passage, a change in scientific advice in light of new evidence shows:
o: That the scientific method is functioning properly
questions.x: Answer: 'That the scientific method is functioning properly'. 'Revision is the method working as it should.' The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Science advances by doubt, yet the public often expects it to deliver certainty. When early advice changes as new evidence arrives, critics call it inconsistency. In fact, revision is the method working as it should. The challenge for scientists is to communicate not only what they know but how confident they are, so that people can tell a firm finding from a reasonable best guess.

questions.q: What does the author want scientists to communicate better?
o: Their level of confidence in a finding
questions.x: Answer: 'Their level of confidence in a finding'. They should say 'how confident they are'. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Science advances by doubt, yet the public often expects it to deliver certainty. When early advice changes as new evidence arrives, critics call it inconsistency. In fact, revision is the method working as it should. The challenge for scientists is to communicate not only what they know but how confident they are, so that people can tell a firm finding from a reasonable best guess.

questions.q: Which of the following best expresses the main idea?
o: Public understanding of science improves when uncertainty is communicated honestly
Doubt has no place in scientific work
The public should stop trusting science
Science should never change its advice
questions.x: Answer: 'Public understanding of science improves when uncertainty is communicated honestly'. The passage is about communicating uncertainty. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Science advances by doubt, yet the public often expects it to deliver certainty. When early advice changes as new evidence arrives, critics call it inconsistency. In fact, revision is the method working as it should. The challenge for scientists is to communicate not only what they know but how confident they are, so that people can tell a firm finding from a reasonable best guess.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Vernacular Press Act, 1878 was called the 'gagging Act'.
Reason (R): It discriminated against Indian-language newspapers by empowering the government to confiscate presses for seditious content.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the integration of princely states:
1. V. P. Menon was Secretary of the States Ministry under Sardar Patel.
2. Under the Instrument of Accession, states ceded defence, external affairs and communications.
3. Hyderabad acceded to India before 15 August 1947.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Hyderabad was integrated after Operation Polo in September 1948.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The All-India Federation proposed by the 1935 Act never came into being.
Reason (R): The required number of princely states did not join it.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q:
Match the school of painting with its region:
School:
A. Kishangarh
B. Basohli
C. Madhubani
D. Pattachitra
Region:
1. Odisha
2. Rajasthan
3. Bihar (Mithila)
4. Pahari (Jammu)
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Kishangarh) → 2 (Rajasthan); B (Basohli) → 4 (Pahari (Jammu)); C (Madhubani) → 3 (Bihar (Mithila)); D (Pattachitra) → 1 (Odisha).
Bani Thani is a famous Kishangarh painting.

questions.q:
Match the text with its author:
Text:
A. Arthashastra
B. Indica
C. Rajatarangini
D. Harshacharita
Author:
1. Banabhatta
2. Megasthenes
3. Kalhana
4. Kautilya
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Arthashastra) → 4 (Kautilya); B (Indica) → 2 (Megasthenes); C (Rajatarangini) → 3 (Kalhana); D (Harshacharita) → 1 (Banabhatta).
Important sources of ancient Indian history.

questions.q:
Consider the following about intangible cultural heritage of India inscribed by UNESCO:
1. Kumbh Mela is inscribed.
2. Durga Puja in Kolkata is inscribed.
3. Garba of Gujarat is inscribed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
Kumbh Mela (2017), Durga Puja (2021), Garba (2023).

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Khilafat movement:
1. It was led by the Ali brothers.
2. It aimed to protect the status of the Ottoman Sultan as Caliph.
3. It ended because Turkey itself abolished the Caliphate in 1924.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Match the movement with its region:
Movement:
A. Pabna agrarian leagues
B. Kuka movement
C. Moplah uprising (1921)
D. Eka movement
Region:
1. East Bengal
2. Malabar
3. Awadh
4. Punjab
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Pabna agrarian leagues) → 1 (East Bengal); B (Kuka movement) → 4 (Punjab); C (Moplah uprising (1921)) → 2 (Malabar); D (Eka movement) → 3 (Awadh).
Peasant and religious-reform movements across regions.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Lucknow Pact (1916) marked a rare phase of Congress–League cooperation.
Reason (R): The Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims in the pact.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true, but R does not explain A. Both are true; R is a term of the pact rather than the reason for cooperation (which arose from the post-war political context and reunification of moderates and extremists).

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Telangana peasant struggle:
1. It was directed against the Nizam's rule and oppressive landlords.
2. Communists played a leading role in it.
3. It ended the day Hyderabad was integrated into India in 1948.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The armed struggle continued until 1951.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Quit India Movement saw the rise of parallel governments in several areas.
Reason (R): With the top Congress leadership arrested on 9 August 1942, the movement became leaderless and decentralised.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Decentralisation allowed local leaders to set up parallel governments (Ballia, Tamluk, Satara).

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Brahmo Samaj:
1. It was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828.
2. It opposed idolatry and sati.
3. It was founded in Bombay.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It was founded in Calcutta.

questions.q:
Consider the following about India's long-term space roadmap:
1. The first module of the Bharatiya Antariksh Station is targeted for 2028.
2. The full station is planned to be operational by 2035.
3. An Indian landing on the Moon is targeted by 2040.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are stated targets of the space roadmap.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): India won the men's hockey Asia Cup in 2025 at Rajgir.
Reason (R): The Asia Cup winner gets a direct berth in the next FIH Hockey World Cup.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true, but R does not explain A. Both are true; R states a consequence, not the reason for the win.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2025:
1. It seeks to decriminalise minor offences by replacing imprisonment with monetary penalties.
2. It follows the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023.
3. It abolishes all penal provisions in central laws.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It amends selected provisions in a set of central Acts; the aim is ease of living and doing business.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Groundwater depletion is severe in north-west India.
Reason (R): Rice cultivation in dry regions is supported by free or subsidised power for pumps.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the 'One Nation One Subscription' scheme:
1. It provides national-level access to international scholarly journals.
2. It covers government higher-education institutions and central government R&D institutions.
3. It is meant only for private universities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It came into effect on 1 January 2025 and is coordinated through INFLIBNET.

questions.q:
Consider the following literary awards:
1. Banu Mushtaq's 'Heart Lamp' won the International Booker Prize 2025.
2. Vinod Kumar Shukla received the 59th Jnanpith Award.
3. Mohanlal received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following about India's fight against tuberculosis:
1. The Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana gives nutritional support to TB patients through direct benefit transfer.
2. India set a goal of ending TB earlier than the SDG target year of 2030.
3. TB is caused by a virus, so antibiotics are not used to treat it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
TB is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis and is treated with a course of antibiotics.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the United Nations in 2025:
1. It marked the 80th anniversary of the UN Charter coming into force.
2. Annalena Baerbock was elected President of the 80th session of the General Assembly.
3. India became a permanent member of the Security Council.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Permanent membership requires Charter amendment; India remains a non-permanent member when elected.

questions.q:
Consider the following EPFO service reforms of 2025:
1. The Centralised Pension Payment System lets EPS pensioners receive pension through any bank branch.
2. A UAN can be generated using Face Authentication Technology through the UMANG app.
3. EPF interest for 2024-25 was fixed at 8.25%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
CPPS went live across EPFO from January 2025.

questions.q:
Consider the following about 'Lakhpati Didi':
1. It aims to help women in self-help groups earn at least ₹1 lakh a year.
2. The target was raised to three crore women.
3. It is implemented under DAY-NRLM.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the UPSC:
1. Its members hold office for six years or until 65 years of age.
2. It is consulted on disciplinary matters affecting civil servants.
3. Its advice is binding on the Government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
UPSC's advice is advisory; the Government must explain non-acceptance to Parliament.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the distribution of legislative powers:
1. Residuary powers rest with Parliament.
2. In case of conflict on a Concurrent List subject, Union law ordinarily prevails.
3. A State law on a Concurrent subject reserved for and assented by the President can prevail in that State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
Article 254(2) permits the State law to prevail in the State.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Public interest litigation relaxed the rule of locus standi.
Reason (R): Courts allowed public-spirited persons to approach them on behalf of those unable to do so.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q: Which of the following is a 'charged' expenditure on the Consolidated Fund of India?
o: Grants to States under centrally sponsored schemes
Salaries and allowances of the Comptroller and Auditor General
questions.x: Charged items include emoluments of the President, Speaker, judges, CAG and debt charges.

questions.q: A sitting MLA is convicted and sentenced to three years' imprisonment. When does disqualification take effect?
o: From the date of conviction, as held in Lily Thomas (2013)
questions.x: Correct answer: From the date of conviction, as held in Lily Thomas (2013). Lily Thomas struck down Section 8(4) of the RPA, 1951.

questions.q:
Consider the following about inter-State water disputes:
1. Article 262 allows Parliament to exclude the Supreme Court's jurisdiction over such disputes.
2. Tribunals are set up under the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956.
3. Water is a subject in the Union List only.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Water is in the State List (Entry 17), subject to Entry 56 of the Union List on inter-State rivers.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The right to property is no longer a Fundamental Right.
Reason (R): The 44th Amendment deleted Article 31 and placed the right to property in Article 300A.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q:
Consider the following about official languages:
1. Hindi in Devanagari script is the official language of the Union under Article 343.
2. English continues to be used for official purposes under the Official Languages Act, 1963.
3. The Eighth Schedule now has 22 languages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): President's Rule can be challenged before the courts.
Reason (R): In S. R. Bommai (1994), the Supreme Court held that the proclamation under Article 356 is subject to judicial review.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the 97th Constitutional Amendment (2011):
1. It added the right to form co-operative societies to Article 19(1)(c).
2. It inserted Article 43B on promoting co-operative societies.
3. In 2021 the Supreme Court upheld Part IXB in full, including provisions on State co-operatives.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Court struck down the parts of Part IXB dealing with State co-operatives for want of State ratification.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the President's rule (Article 356):
1. It must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within two months.
2. Once approved it continues for six months, and can be extended up to three years with conditions after the first year.
3. The State Legislative Assembly is always dissolved when it is imposed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Assembly may be kept in suspended animation.

questions.q:
Consider the following about ordinances:
1. The President can promulgate an ordinance only when both Houses are not in session or one is not in session.
2. An ordinance can amend the Constitution.
3. An ordinance lapses six weeks after the reassembly of Parliament unless approved.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect; Statement 3 is correct.
An ordinance cannot amend the Constitution.

questions.q:
With reference to the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana, consider the following:
1. It provides collateral-free loans to non-corporate, non-farm micro enterprises.
2. The 'Tarun Plus' category extends loans up to ₹20 lakh for those who have repaid Tarun loans.
3. MUDRA loans are disbursed directly by the Ministry of Finance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Loans are given by banks, NBFCs and MFIs; MUDRA refinances them.

questions.q:
Which of the following are recorded in the current account of India's balance of payments?
1. Remittances from Indians working abroad
2. Earnings of Indian IT firms from software exports
3. Investment by a foreign company to set up a factory in India
4. Interest paid on India's external debt
How many of the above?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
FDI is a financial/capital account item.

questions.q: In a simple banking model, the cash reserve ratio is 10% and banks keep no excess reserves. A fresh deposit of ₹900 crore can lead to a maximum total deposit creation of:
questions.x:
Deposit (money) multiplier = 1 / CRR = 1 / 0.1 = 10.
Total deposits = 900 × 10 = ₹9,000 crore (of which new credit = ₹8,100 crore).

questions.q:
Consider the following about national income aggregates:
1. GDP at market prices = GVA at basic prices + product taxes − product subsidies.
2. NNP = GNP − depreciation.
3. GNP is always larger than GDP for India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
India's net factor income from abroad is usually negative, so GNP is generally smaller than GDP.

questions.q: Gross profit ratio is 25% on sales of ₹8,00,000. Opening stock ₹90,000; closing stock ₹1,10,000. Inventory turnover ratio is:
questions.x: COGS = 75% × 8,00,000 = ₹6,00,000; average stock = ₹1,00,000; turnover = 6 times.

questions.q: Sales of ₹14,500 to Mohan were correctly entered in the sales book but posted to Mohan's account as ₹15,400. The effect on the trial balance is:
o: Debit side exceeds credit side by ₹900
Debit side exceeds credit side by ₹1,800
Credit side exceeds debit side by ₹900
questions.x: Correct answer: Debit side exceeds credit side by ₹900. Sales credited ₹14,500; Mohan debited ₹15,400 — excess debit of ₹900.

questions.q: A firm has Cash ₹40,000, Debtors ₹65,000, Inventory ₹40,000, Prepaid expenses ₹5,000, Creditors ₹55,000, Bills payable ₹5,000 and Outstanding expenses ₹10,000. Its quick (acid-test) ratio is:
questions.x:
Quick assets exclude inventory and prepaid expenses: 40,000 + 65,000 = ₹1,05,000.
Current liabilities = ₹70,000.
Quick ratio = 1,05,000 / 70,000 = 1.5 : 1 (benchmark 1 : 1).

questions.q: Operating profit is best computed as:
o: Gross profit − operating expenses (administration, selling and distribution) + operating incomes
questions.x: Non-operating items such as interest received or loss on sale of assets are excluded.

questions.q:
Which of the following costs are excluded from the cost of inventories under AS 2 and recognised as expenses?
1. Administrative overheads that do not contribute to bringing inventories to their present location and condition
2. Abnormal amounts of wasted materials
3. Freight inward on raw materials
4. Selling and distribution costs
Which of the above are excluded?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect; Statement 4 is correct.
Freight inward is part of the purchase cost and is included in inventory cost.

questions.q: A machine costs ₹5,00,000 with residual value ₹50,000 and life 9 years under SLM. At the start of year 4, its remaining useful life is re-estimated at 3 years with the same residual value. Depreciation from year 4 onwards is:
questions.x: Annual SLM = 4,50,000/9 = ₹50,000. After 3 years, book value = ₹3,50,000; depreciable = 3,00,000 over 3 years = ₹1,00,000 per year (a change in estimate is applied prospectively).

questions.q: Opening inventory is ₹65,000, closing inventory is ₹90,000 and cost of goods sold for the year is ₹6,20,000. The inventory turnover ratio is:
questions.x:
Average inventory = (65,000 + 90,000) / 2 = ₹77,500.
Inventory turnover = COGS / Average inventory = 6,20,000 / 77,500 = 8 times.

questions.q:
Consider the following about statutory audit of companies in India:
1. The auditor is appointed at the AGM for a term from one AGM to the sixth AGM.
2. Listed companies must rotate individual auditors after one term of five years.
3. The Comptroller and Auditor General appoints auditors of government companies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three reflect Sections 139 and 139(5) of the Companies Act, 2013.

questions.q: From the following, compute Gross Profit: Opening stock ₹55,000; Purchases ₹2,95,000; Purchase returns ₹1,000; Carriage inwards ₹2,000; Sales ₹3,38,500; Sales returns ₹2,000; Closing stock ₹30,000.
questions.x:
Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases − Purchase returns + Carriage inwards − Closing stock
= 55,000 + 2,95,000 − 1,000 + 2,000 − 30,000 = ₹3,21,000.
Gross profit = Net sales − COGS = 3,38,500 − 2,000 − 3,21,000 = ₹15,500.
Carriage inwards is a direct expense (Trading A/c).

questions.q: Fixed costs are ₹1,20,000, selling price ₹50 and variable cost ₹30 per unit. Actual sales are 9,000 units. The margin of safety in units is:
Goods worth ₹1,00,000 are insured with two insurers for ₹60,000 and ₹40,000. A loss of ₹50,000 occurs. Under the principle of contribution, the second insurer pays:
Fixed costs are ₹59,000; selling price ₹155 and variable cost ₹145 per unit. How many units must be sold to earn a profit of ₹5,000?
questions.x:
Required units = (Fixed cost + Target profit) / Contribution per unit
= (59,000 + 5,000) / 10 = 6,400 units.

questions.q: A firm wants to determine the relative worth of different jobs to design a fair pay structure. The appropriate tool is:
questions.x: Job evaluation ranks jobs; appraisal rates people.

questions.q:
With reference to bonus under the Code on Wages, consider the following:
1. An employee who has worked for at least thirty days in the accounting year is eligible.
2. Bonus is payable at a minimum of 8.33% even if the establishment incurs a loss.
3. A person dismissed for sexual harassment can be disqualified from receiving bonus.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct: minimum bonus is payable regardless of allocable surplus, and the Code added sexual harassment as a disqualification ground.

questions.q: A worker's wage is ₹500 per day. The employer fines ₹300 in a month of 26 working days for damage to goods, with prior approval of the act. Under the Code on Wages, the maximum fine permissible in that wage period is:
questions.x: Wages for the period = 500 × 26 = ₹13,000; 3% = ₹390. A fine of ₹300 is within the cap.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 originally required notice of strike only in public utility services.
Reason (R): The Act's First Schedule listed industries that could be declared public utility services.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true, but R does not explain A. Both statements are true; the First Schedule enabled declarations, but that is not the reason the notice rule was confined to public utilities.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the ILO:
1. It is the only tripartite UN agency, with governments, employers and workers represented.
2. Each member sends two government, one employer and one worker delegate to the International Labour Conference.
3. Its conventions are binding on a member State even without ratification.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Conventions bind only on ratification; the 1998 Declaration creates an obligation to respect fundamental principles.

questions.q:
Match the earlier law with the Code that subsumed it:
Old law:
A. Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Cess Act, 1996
B. Building and Other Construction Workers (RE&CS) Act, 1996
C. Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946
D. Equal Remuneration Act, 1976
Code:
1. IR Code
2. OSH Code
3. Code on Wages
4. Code on Social Security
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Cess Act, 1996) → 4 (Code on Social Security); B (Building and Other Construction Workers (RE&CS) Act, 1996) → 2 (OSH Code); C (Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946) → 1 (IR Code); D (Equal Remuneration Act, 1976) → 3 (Code on Wages).
Note the split: the BOCW Cess Act went into the Code on Social Security while the BOCW regulation Act went into the OSH Code.

questions.q:
With reference to the Bangalore Water Supply case (1978), consider the following:
1. It laid down the 'triple test' of systematic activity, employer–employee co-operation and production of goods or services.
2. It held that charitable hospitals can never be an industry.
3. It was decided by a seven-judge bench.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect; Statement 3 is correct.
The case adopted the dominant nature test and held that even charitable activities can be industry if the triple test is met; the IR Code later excluded certain wholly charitable institutions by statute.

questions.q:
Consider the following concepts of wages:
1. A minimum wage should provide for bare subsistence and preservation of efficiency.
2. A living wage is the ideal that also provides for education, health and insurance.
3. A fair wage is always higher than the living wage.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Committee on Fair Wages (1948) placed the fair wage between the minimum and the living wage, depending on the capacity of the industry.

questions.q: A suspended worker's inquiry is delayed beyond 90 days for reasons not attributable to the worker. Under the IR Code, subsistence allowance after the first 90 days becomes:
questions.x: Subsistence allowance is 50% for the first 90 days and 75% thereafter if the delay is not due to the worker.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan is called a 'contributory' pension scheme.
Reason (R): The Government makes a matching contribution equal to the subscriber's contribution.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true, but R does not explain A. Both are true. A is about its contributory nature (subscriber pays); R explains the matching but not why it is called contributory.

questions.q: Which feature distinguishes voluntary arbitration from adjudication under the IR Code?
o: Adjudication is conducted by the trade union
Arbitration rests on a written agreement of the parties; adjudication follows a reference or an application under the Code
Arbitration is available only in public utility services
questions.x: Section 42 provides for voluntary reference to arbitration by written agreement.

questions.q: Which feature of the Labour Codes reduces discretionary 'inspector raj'?
o: Web-based, randomised inspection schemes run by Inspector-cum-Facilitators
questions.x: The Codes provide for randomised, web-based inspection and a facilitative role for inspectors.

questions.q: A union has 450 members in a 5,000-worker establishment and applies for registration. Under the IR Code, the application:
o: Qualifies, since 100 workers or 10% — whichever is less — is enough
Fails, as 51% membership is required for registration
Fails, as 10% of 5,000 (500) members are needed
Qualifies only if the employer consents
questions.x: The threshold is 10% or 100 workers, whichever is less — here 100. With 450 members, it qualifies.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The OSH Code treats audio-visual workers in digital productions as covered workers.
Reason (R): The Cine-Workers and Cinema Theatre Workers Act, 1981 covered only cinema theatres.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true but R is false. A is correct. R is false — the 1981 Act covered cine workers in film production as well as cinema theatre workers.

questions.q: Which combination of constitutional provisions has been used by courts to develop the principle of 'equal pay for equal work'?
questions.x: Randhir Singh (1982) read the DPSP in Article 39(d) with Articles 14 and 16.

questions.q:
Which of the following are excluded from the definition of 'industry' under the IR Code, 2020?
1. Domestic service
2. A charitable hospital wholly run by an organisation engaged in philanthropic service
3. A commercial bank
4. Defence research activities of a government department
How many of the above are excluded?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Domestic service, purely charitable/philanthropic institutions and sovereign functions including defence research, atomic energy and space are excluded; a commercial bank is an industry.

questions.q:
Consider the following about social security standards:
1. The Beveridge Report of 1942 laid the foundation of the British welfare state.
2. ILO Convention No. 102 (1952) sets minimum standards for social security.
3. India has ratified ILO Convention No. 102.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
India has not ratified Convention 102.

questions.q: Under the Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995, a member retires at 58 with pensionable salary of ₹12,000 and pensionable service of 15 years (including any weightage). The monthly member pension is:
questions.x:
Monthly pension = (Pensionable salary × Pensionable service) / 70
= (12,000 × 15) / 70 = ₹2,571.
Pensionable salary is the average of the last 60 months' wages (subject to the ₹15,000 ceiling), and the minimum pension is ₹1,000.

questions.q: An employee retires after 14 years and 9 months of continuous service. Last drawn monthly wages (basic + DA) are ₹63,000. Gratuity payable under the statutory formula (non-seasonal establishment) is:
questions.x:
Gratuity = 15/26 × last drawn wages × completed years of service.
9 months is more than six months, so it counts as a full year → 15 years.
= 15/26 × 63,000 × 15 = ₹5,45,192 (well within the ₹20 lakh ceiling).
The divisor 26 reflects working days in a month.

questions.q: A member with pensionable salary ₹15,000 and 30 years' service (including weightage) retires at 58. Another member with the same salary and 9 years' service leaves. What do they get?
o: First gets ₹6,429 monthly pension; second gets a withdrawal benefit or scheme certificate
questions.x: 15,000 × 30 / 70 = ₹6,428.57 ≈ ₹6,429; with less than ten years of service, no monthly pension is payable.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): NPS is a defined contribution scheme.
Reason (R): In NPS, the pension depends on contributions and the returns earned on them.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q: A worker earning ₹14,000 a month is covered by both EPF and ESI. The employee's total statutory monthly deduction for these two is:
An employee's basic + DA is ₹24,000. Employer and employee contribute on the statutory wage ceiling only. The monthly amounts credited to the member's EPF account and EPS account respectively are:
questions.x: On ₹15,000: employee 12% = ₹1,800 (EPF); employer 12% = ₹1,800, of which ₹1,250 goes to EPS and ₹550 to EPF. EPF total = ₹2,350.

questions.q: An employee's last drawn wage is ₹52,000 per month and service is 34 years 8 months. Statutory gratuity payable is:
questions.x: 15/26 × 52,000 = ₹30,000 per year; 8 months > 6 months, so 35 years: 30,000 × 35 = ₹10,50,000 (within the ₹20 lakh cap).

questions.q:
Which of the following are benefits provided under the ESI Act?
1. Sickness benefit
2. Dependants' benefit
3. Funeral expenses
4. Housing benefit
How many of the above are ESI benefits?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Housing is not an ESI benefit. The benefits are medical, sickness, maternity, disablement, dependants', funeral expenses and unemployment allowance schemes.

questions.q: A woman employee entitled to 26 weeks of maternity benefit has an average daily wage of ₹770. Following the Supreme Court's view in B. Shah v. Presiding Officer (1977) that the benefit covers all days of the period, the total maternity benefit is:
questions.x:
The benefit is paid for every day of the 26-week period including Sundays: 26 × 7 = 182 days.
Amount = ₹770 × 182 = ₹1,40,140. (Using 6 days/week would wrongly give ₹1,20,120.)

questions.q:
Consider the following about sound:
1. Sound cannot travel through a vacuum.
2. Sound travels faster in steel than in air.
3. Ultrasound has frequencies below 20 Hz.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Ultrasound is above 20 kHz; below 20 Hz is infrasound.

questions.q: A 4-bit register stores numbers in two's complement form. What is the range of values it can hold?
questions.x: Correct answer: −8 to +7. n bits in two's complement hold −2ⁿ⁻¹ to 2ⁿ⁻¹ − 1.

questions.q:
Consider the following about tides:
1. Spring tides occur at new moon and full moon.
2. Neap tides occur when the Sun and Moon are at right angles relative to the Earth.
3. The Sun's tidal effect is stronger than the Moon's.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Moon's tidal effect is about twice the Sun's because it is much nearer.

questions.q: In a spreadsheet, cell B2 contains the formula =A2*$C$1. It is copied to B5. What will the formula in B5 be?
questions.x: A2 is relative and shifts down three rows; $C$1 is absolute and does not change.

questions.q:
Consider the following about stem cells:
1. They can divide and develop into specialised cell types.
2. Umbilical cord blood is a source of blood-forming stem cells.
3. Adult bodies contain no stem cells.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Adults have stem cells, e.g., in bone marrow.

questions.q:
Consider the following about malware:
1. A worm can spread across networks without attaching itself to a host file.
2. A Trojan horse disguises itself as useful software.
3. A virus spreads on its own without any host program.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
A virus attaches itself to a host file or program; self-spreading malware is a worm.

questions.q:
Consider the following about carbolic acid:
1. Chemically it is phenol.
2. Joseph Lister used it as an antiseptic in surgery.
3. It is a strong mineral acid like sulphuric acid.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Phenol is a weak organic acid.

questions.q:
Consider the following about food preservation:
1. Pasteurisation heats milk to kill harmful microbes without boiling it.
2. Irradiation makes food radioactive.
3. Refrigeration slows the growth of microbes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect; Statement 3 is correct.
Irradiated food does not become radioactive.

questions.q:
Consider the following about India's digital public infrastructure:
1. UPI allows instant transfers between bank accounts using a virtual payment address.
2. DigiLocker documents are legally valid like the originals under the IT rules.
3. Aadhaar Enabled Payment System lets users transact using Aadhaar and biometric authentication.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Electricity is transmitted over long distances at very high voltage.
Reason (R): For the same power, a higher voltage means a lower current and lower I²R losses in the lines.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Transformers make this possible for AC.

questions.q:
Consider the following species in India:
1. Lantana camara
2. Prosopis juliflora
3. Water hyacinth
4. Neem
How many of the above are invasive alien species in India?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Neem is native to the Indian subcontinent.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the colours of hydrogen:
1. Green hydrogen is produced by electrolysis of water using renewable electricity.
2. Grey hydrogen is produced from natural gas without capturing the carbon dioxide.
3. Blue hydrogen is produced by electrolysis using nuclear power.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Blue hydrogen is from fossil fuels with carbon capture; hydrogen from nuclear power is often called pink.

questions.q:
Consider the following about blood groups:
1. A person with group O negative is often called a universal donor of red cells.
2. A person with group AB positive can usually receive red cells from any ABO and Rh group.
3. Rh incompatibility can affect a baby when the mother is Rh positive and the foetus is Rh negative.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The risk arises when the mother is Rh negative and the foetus is Rh positive.

questions.q: The ratio of the present ages of P and Q is 7 : 3. After 11 years, the ratio will become 25 : 17. What is P's present age?
Find the remainder when 5^197 is divided by 13.
A train 140 m long running at 54 km/h crosses a platform in 31 seconds. The length of the platform is:
questions.x:
Speed = 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s. Distance covered in 31 s = 465 m = train + platform.
Platform = 465 − 140 = 325 m.

questions.q: ₹27,000 is invested for 1 year at 20% per annum, interest being compounded half-yearly. The compound interest earned is:
questions.x:
Half-yearly: rate per period = 20/2 = 10%, number of periods = 2.
Amount = 27,000 × (1 + 10/100)² = ₹32,670.
CI = ₹5,670 (slightly more than annual compounding, which gives ₹5,400).

questions.q: Ravi can digitise a set of records in 16 days and Kiran in 48 days. They start together, but Ravi leaves after 9 days. In how many days in all is the work completed?
questions.x:
Work done together in 9 days = 9 × (1/16 + 1/48) = 9/12 = 3/4.
Remaining = 1/4, done by Kiran alone in 1/4 × 48 = 12 days.
Total = 9 + 12 = 21 days.

questions.q:
Members enrolled in a district (thousand) — 2018: 200  |  2019: 180  |  2020: 175  |  2021: 150  |  2022: 185.
In which year was the percentage growth over the previous year the highest?
questions.x:
Year-on-year growth: 2019: -10%; 2020: -2.78%; 2021: -14.29%; 2022: 23.33%.
Highest growth: 2022 (23.33%). Note: the largest absolute rise need not be the largest percentage rise.

questions.q: An article is marked 60% above its cost. Two successive discounts of 10% and 5% are then given on the marked price. The resulting gain or loss per cent is:
questions.x:
Take CP = 100 → MP = 160.
After 10%: 144; after a further 5%: 136.8.
Net = 136.8 − 100 = 36.8 → 36.8% gain.
Successive discounts are multiplied, never added (10% + 5% ≠ 15%).

questions.q: Given log₁₀ 2 = 0.301, how many digits are there in 2^54?
questions.x:
log₁₀(2^54) = 54 × log₁₀ 2 = 54 × 0.301 = 16.2540.
The characteristic is 16, so the number of digits = 16 + 1 = 17.

questions.q: A starts a business with ₹30,000. B joins after 2 months with ₹30,000, and C joins after 6 months with ₹35,000. Out of a year-end profit of ₹37,700, B's share is:
questions.x:
Profit is shared in the ratio of capital × time.
A: 30,000×12, B: 30,000×10, C: 35,000×6 → 12 : 10 : 7.
B's share = 10/29 × 37,700 = ₹13,000.

questions.q: On which day of the week did 15 June 2053 fall?
questions.x:
Odd-day method (Sunday = 0).
Completed years = 2052: 2000 years → 0 odd days; 0 years → 0; remaining 52 years have 13 leap + 39 ordinary → 13×2 + 39 = 65 → 2 odd day(s).
Days elapsed in 2053 up to 15 June = 166 → 5 odd day(s).
Total = 0 + 2 + 5 = 7 → 0 → Sunday.

questions.q: Two trains start at the same time from stations X and Y towards each other. After they cross, they take 25 hours and 9 hours respectively to reach Y and X. The ratio of the speed of the train from X to that of the train from Y is:
questions.x:
Standard result: S₁ : S₂ = √t₂ : √t₁, where t₁ and t₂ are the times taken after meeting.
= √9 : √25 = 3 : 5 = 3 : 5.

questions.q: How many arrangements of the letters of 'COMPANY' are there in which the vowels are NOT all together?
questions.x:
Total arrangements = 5,040 (all letters are distinct).
Vowels together = 720 × 2 = 1,440.
Not all together = 5,040 − 1,440 = 3,600.

questions.q: A bus runs from town P to town Q at 84 km/h and returns along the same road at 112 km/h. The average speed for the whole journey is:
questions.x:
For equal distances, average speed = 2uv/(u + v) (harmonic mean), not (u + v)/2.
= 2 × 84 × 112 / (84 + 112) = 18816/196 = 96 km/h.

questions.q: In a certain code, 'A $ B' means A is the father of B; 'A − B' means A is the mother of B; 'A % B' means A is the daughter of B; 'A + B' means A is the wife of B. If 'T $ Q − K' (read as T $ Q and Q − K), how is T related to K?
questions.x:
T $ Q: T is the father of Q. Q − K: Q is the mother of K.
Combining the two (all persons taken to be of one family, as is conventional): T is the maternal grandfather of K.

questions.q: Find the greatest number that will divide 457, 597, 807 leaving the same remainder in each case.
questions.x:
If N leaves the same remainder, N divides the differences.
Differences: 597 − 457 = 140, 807 − 597 = 210.
HCF(140, 210) = 70.
